aiOverview.content: The Artemis II mission itself is estimated to cost approximately $4.1 billion to $4.2 billion per launch. This cost covers the operation of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the Orion crew capsule, with total program expenditures, including development, expected to exceed $100 billion by the time humans land on the moon again.Launch Cost: The NASA Inspector General estimated the cost per individual launch (like Artemis II) to be around $4.1 billion in a 2021/2022 projection.Total Program Cost: The overall Artemis program is frequently cited to cost over $90-$100 billion by the mid-2020s.Development Cost: Combined, the Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft have cost more than $44 billion to develop.The high cost is due to the complexity of developing the hardware, which serves as a major effort to bring humans back around the moon for the first time in over 50 years. The Artemis II mission itself is estimated to cost approximately $4.1 billion to $4.2 billion per launch. This cost covers the operation of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the Orion crew capsule, with total program expenditures, including development, expected to exceed $100 billion by the time humans land on the moon again. Launch Cost: The NASA Inspector General estimated the cost per individual launch (like Artemis II) to be around $4.1 billion in a 2021/2022 projection. Total Program Cost: The overall Artemis program is frequently cited to cost over $90-$100 billion by the mid-2020s. Development Cost: Combined, the Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft have cost more than $44 billion to develop. The high cost is due to the complexity of developing the hardware, which serves as a major effort to bring humans back around the moon for the first time in over 50 years.
